sources.entry: Clave - macOS app for managing multiple Claude Code sessions in parallel, with split/grid layouts, session groups, SSH remote sessions, a git panel, and usage analytics.

summary.one_liner: Clave is a macOS (and early Windows) desktop app for running and managing multiple coding-agent CLI sessions in parallel, arranged in split or grid layouts.
summary.what_it_does: Clave runs Claude Code, Antigravity CLI, Codex CLI, and Pi sessions side by side, each in its own PTY, plus plain terminals. Sessions can be arranged in split or grid layouts and switched between quickly. It includes a built-in git panel with diff viewer, commit history, and a one-click flow to pull, stage, write an AI commit message, commit, and push. Users can link Markdown, HTML, or structured email drafts to a session and edit them in a two-pane view. Local and remote files can be browsed and edited over SSH/SFTP, and agents can be run on remote hosts over SSH. The README also describes a companion agent plugin that generates .clave workspace files and recovers sessions from Claude Code transcripts.
use_cases: run several Claude Code sessions at once
manage parallel coding agents in one window
arrange agent terminals in split or grid layouts
run AI coding agents on remote hosts over SSH
git commits and diffs alongside agent sessions
recover lost agent sessions after a crash
how_to_run: Download the .dmg from the latest GitHub release and drag Clave to Applications
npm run dev  (development with hot reload)
npm run build:mac  (builds macOS .dmg; requires signing credentials)
notable: Provider-agnostic: works with Claude Code, Antigravity CLI, Codex CLI, and Pi sessions
Fully local desktop app with no cloud backend or account
Companion agent plugin that generates .clave workspace files (Claude Code, Cursor, and other Open-Plugin hosts)
Remote sessions and file editing over SSH/SFTP using the same UI
Dangerous Mode (Cmd+D) is opt-in and clearly labelled
caveats: Windows support is early and unsigned: agent state dots and tmux-backed session persistence are macOS-only, and Pi sessions are not available
Requires at least one supported agent CLI installed and authenticated
Building the macOS .dmg requires signing credentials; the README includes a detailed keychain workaround for its release pipeline
Sends one anonymous usage ping per day by default (can be turned off in Settings)
